observation.visible_scene: A low-angle close-up of a road-roller drum resting on grey asphalt. Visible parts: a yellow mounting bracket at the upper-left, a rusty circular hub with bolt holes at the centre, a large dark curved metal shell forming the drum body, and a thin black flap/scraper protruding from the right edge of the shell. The rig is moving over the pavement throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The asphalt texture and a small piece of leaf/debris near the bottom of the frame drift steadily downward and out of view, and the green grass and curb at the upper-right exit the frame within the first few frames, indicating continuous forward translation of the roller-camera assembly.
The drum, hub and black flap stay at an approximately constant position within the frame, so the camera travels with the roller rather than the drum sliding across a fixed viewpoint.

The black flap on the drum's right edge changes its outline slightly between frames (bending, with a small notch near its base appearing and disappearing), consistent with a flexible part fluttering while remaining attached.
The yellow bracket at the upper-left shifts gradually upward in the frame as the segment progresses.
The dark shell's faint white scratch near its lower-left stays in the same place relative to the drum, so no obvious rotation of that surface is visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the drum is actually rotating: surface marks appear nearly stationary relative to the frame, so the dark curved shell may be a fixed shield/fender, or rotation is too slow or too blurred to confirm from these samples.
The cause of the flap's flutter, the machine's speed, and any events before the first frame or after the last frame.
The material identity of the black flap and the dark shell.
uncertain_details: Exact drum rotation versus a stationary shield.
Whether the slight vertical drift of frame contents is camera tilt, camera pan, or roller motion.
Precise shape changes of the flap (could be deformation, flutter, or partial occlusion by the shell edge).
